label: 2025 Homicide Rate (Record High)
contestNote: Independent trackers agree 2025 was the deadliest year on record, up 31% from 2024; government and academic tallies have historically diverged in methodology for classifying conflict-related deaths.
deltaNote: Highest homicide rate recorded since at least 2014, making Ecuador the most homicidal country in Latin America for a third consecutive year.

label: 2024 Homicide Rate
contestNote: Estimates vary by methodology: some sources report a 14% decline from 2023's 45.7/100k to ~39.3/100k in 2024, while others (Statista/Macrotrends) cite a rate as high as 46.5/100k — an eightfold increase from 5.8/100k in 2018.

label: International Tourist Arrivals (2024)
source: Ecuador Ministry of Tourism / Focus on Travel News
deltaNote: Down 43.4% from 2019's pre-pandemic peak of ~2.5 million visitors; Galápagos visits fell 26% in the same period.

label: Attacks on Journalists (2024)
deltaNote: At least 15 journalists went into exile in the two years to 2025; 11 media workers have been killed since 2021.

label: Excessive Force Complaints Filed (2024)
contestNote: Highest figure in at least a decade; complaints remained elevated at 249 in 2025. The government disputes characterizations of systematic abuse, framing incidents as isolated and under investigation.
